data.name: Cayman Islands
data.summary: The Cayman Islands has no income, capital gains, dividend, inheritance, estate, gift, wealth or property tax. The real costs are stamp duty on buying Cayman land (7.5%, and 10% from 1 January 2026 for property worth CI$2 million or more) and nominal probate fees for Cayman-situs assets. No tax treaties. Wealthy foreigners usually reside under the 25-year Residency Certificate for persons of independent means (CI$1 million investment, at least CI$500,000 in developed real estate, CI$120,000 annual income).

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.eligibility: Any lawful resident; non-Caymanians need a residency certificate or other permission from WORC.

capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on transfers of Cayman land: 7.5% for non-Caymanian buyers, on the higher of price and market value; from 1 January 2026 10% where the value is CI$2 million or more (Stamp Duty (Rates of Duty) (No. 2) Regulations 2025). Share transfers in land-holding companies follow the same 7.5%/10%. Mortgages: 1% up to CI$300,000, 1.5% above. First-time Caymanian buyer concessions (exempt up to CI$550,000 from February 2025) do not apply to non-Caymanians.

open_questions: Whether stamp duty applies when Cayman land vests in heirs on death (transmission). PwC (reviewed 29 May 2026) gives stamp duty of generally 7.5% on transfers of Cayman immovable property and on shares in land-holding companies, but does not address transfers on death or to family; the Stamp Duty Act schedule was not read. other_transfer_cost_rate is kept at 0 pending a primary source.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Transfers of Cayman land between certain family members for natural love and affection are exempt from stamp duty under the Stamp Duty Act (relationships not listed in the source).
inheritance.domicile_rules: No transfer taxes; domicile irrelevant locally.

residency.tax_residency_test: No direct taxes; tax residence has no local consequence.

routes.name: 25-year Residency Certificate (persons of independent means)
routes.requirements: Grand Cayman: CI$1,000,000 investment of which at least CI$500,000 in developed real estate, plus annual income of at least CI$120,000 without local employment (or a local deposit of CI$400,000). Fees: CI$500 application, CI$50,000 grant, CI$3,000 per dependant; annual declaration CI$500 + CI$3,000 per dependant. Cayman Brac/Little Cayman: CI$500,000 (CI$250,000 real estate), CI$75,000 income. No right to work. Minimum 30 days' presence per calendar year (Bedell Cristin). Thresholds are 'expected to increase significantly' (Cayman Resident, Oct 2026).

routes.name: Certificate of Permanent Residence (persons of independent means)
routes.requirements: Investment in developed real estate of CI$2 million or more (Bedell Cristin 2023; amount not confirmed on an official page). Loss of status if ordinarily resident abroad for a year or more.

routes.name: Certificate of Direct Investment / Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence)
routes.requirements: For investors in employment-generating businesses or owners of at least 10% of an approved business; 90 days' annual presence. Amounts not researched.

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens stay subject to US federal tax on worldwide income, gains and estate; with no local income tax there is no local tax to credit, so the US layer applies in full. No income tax treaty with the US.
open_questions: An October 2025 Immigration reform bill (Cayman Compass) may change investor-residency thresholds; article could not be opened and current WORC figures were not verified on an official page.

No indicator overrides: the Cayman Islands is in the World Bank/WGI data (homicide rate 2020, internet users 2017, life expectancy 2024), so under the research guide no override is added; RCIPS annual crime statistics were not retrieved to check for a newer homicide figure. UNDP publishes no HDI and TI no CPI for the Cayman Islands; there is no same-definition substitute, so the hdi and corruption composites stay unscored.

income.name: Cayman Islands

income_tax.summary: No income, withholding, payroll or social security taxes on individuals. The only mandatory contribution is the national pension: 5% from the employee (matched by the employer) up to CI$87,000 of earnings, or 10% for the self-employed.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: National Pensions Act s.47: the self-employed must contribute 10% of earnings up to the year's maximum pensionable earnings to a pension plan. The Act's default maximum is CI$87,000, 'or such other amount as may be prescribed by Order'; no Order for 2026 was found. Mandatory health insurance (employer pays at least half of the premium) is not included because the employee share was not verified.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No income tax of any kind (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026). Work-permit holders must also be covered by health insurance; that cost is not modelled.

regimes.name: Global Citizen Concierge Program (closed)
regimes.description: CLOSED. Remote-work certificate launched in October 2020 that let employees of non-Cayman employers live in the Cayman Islands for up to 24 months. The Immigration (Transition) (Global Citizen Exemption) Regulations stopped accepting applications on 31 October 2022 and expired on 30 November 2024 (Maples, 2021 amendment); the Tourism Minister said the programme was 'no longer available as of October 2022' (Caribbean Journal 2023). No relaunch was found, so it is listed for history only and not counted as an open route. The Cayman Islands has no income tax, so the certificate affected access only.
regimes.duration_note: Up to 24 months per Maples (Nov 2021). Currently not open to new applicants. Income threshold of USD 100,000 (USD 150,000 with a spouse) comes from search-result summaries of 2020-21 coverage, not from a page opened here.

succession.name: Cayman Islands
succession.summary: The Cayman Islands have no forced heirship. Cayman trusts are protected by statute against foreign forced-heirship claims and a foundation company (2017) is available. The Hague Trusts Convention is not listed as extended to Cayman.
succession.foreign_law_note: Immovable property in Cayman is governed by Cayman law; movable property follows the law of the deceased's domicile (Ogier, via search summary). There is no choice of nationality law.
succession.trust_note: Cayman is not on the UK's HCCH extension list. Trusts Act (2021 Revision): courts will not recognise forced-heirship claims against a Cayman trust (foreign-element provisions, since 1987); s. 90 governing law. STAR trusts allow purpose trusts. Foundation Companies Act (2017) applies Trusts Act ss. 92-93 to contributed property.
open_questions: Sources conflict on family provision: one guide says dependants may claim under the 1975-style Act, Ogier says Cayman courts cannot award dependants out of an estate. Succession Act 2021 Revision not read in full.
The firewall sections quoted from secondary summaries; primary text not read.

immigration.name: Cayman Islands
immigration.summary: The Cayman Islands offer a 25-year renewable residency certificate (CI$1 million invested plus CI$120,000 income, CI$50,000 fee, no right to work) and a certificate of permanent residence for CI$2 million of property (CI$200,000 fee, work allowed), both revised on 1 May 2026. The remote-worker programme (Global Citizen Concierge) is closed. No direct taxes. EU, US and other passports use the same routes.
immigration.naturalisation: Not recorded: no verified current rule. A CPR holder may later qualify for a path to Cayman and British citizenship after indefinite renewal, under separate residence requirements (Bedell Cristin).
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Not source-checked; British Overseas Territories citizenship generally allows dual nationality.

routes.name: Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means (CER)
routes.summary: A 25-year, renewable residence certificate for CI$1,000,000 invested (half in Grand Cayman real estate) plus CI$120,000 a year of income. No right to work. Amended on 1 May 2026.
routes.requirements: Grand Cayman: invest at least CI$1,000,000 (half in developed Grand Cayman real estate) and show annual income of at least CI$120,000 or CI$400,000 in qualifying assets with a Cayman-regulated institution. Cayman Brac and Little Cayman: CI$500,000 (half in local developed real estate) and CI$75,000 income or CI$400,000 assets. Age 18+, no serious convictions, good health and adequate insurance. One-time approval fee CI$50,000; CI$3,000 a year per dependant. Valid 25 years, renewable; holder and spouse may not work; no direct path to Cayman or British citizenship. No requirement to give up other residencies.
routes.investment_options: CI$500,000 (CI$250,000 in real estate) for Cayman Brac and Little Cayman with CI$75,000 income.
routes.fees_note: One-time approval fee; CI$3,000 a year per dependant. The CI$500 application fee reported elsewhere was not reconfirmed.
routes.tax_note: The Cayman Islands levy no direct taxes on individuals.

routes.name: Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means (CPR)
routes.summary: A residence certificate for investing CI$2 million (US$2.44 million) in one developed Cayman property. Ten-year initial term, then indefinite renewal; the holder may work. Rules changed on 1 May 2026.
routes.requirements: Equity investment of at least CI$2m (US$2.44m) in a single qualifying developed real estate asset in the Cayman Islands; sufficient prescribed financial resources; good health and insurance; no serious convictions. Initial 10 years; after 9 years the holder may apply to renew indefinitely. One-time approval fee CI$200,000; CI$3,000 a year per dependant. Permits holder and spouse to reside and work. After indefinite renewal it may support a pathway to Cayman and British citizenship under separate requirements.
routes.fees_note: One-time approval fee; CI$3,000 a year per dependant.
routes.physical_presence: At least one day each year
routes.tax_note: The Cayman Islands levy no direct taxes on individuals.

routes.summary: A certificate for remote workers earning USD 100,000 a year. It stopped accepting applications on 31 October 2022 and its regulations expired on 30 November 2024.
